assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_KANA_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (22,613 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, do_not_use_as_current_authority false), a portrait of Kana (カナ; 堅 香子) confined to Asaura's Japanese Ordinary days, chiefly Introduction 5 (S17) and the fifth story 『ご注文は？』 (S18), with earlier café appearances (S10, S15), the second-story train encounter (S12) and S19 separately attributed, located by spine item and paragraph. Its closing paragraphs state which conditions should bring curiosity, humor and a return visit and what a nod or silence under threat does not signify. The discovery row claims behavior, psychology, ethics, relationships and decision-making, and does not claim speech; the portrait describes her register shifts briefly without a performed voice. She has no television identity. The Ordinary days reading the portrait links is not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on it directly. The project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Ordinary days only. Her history belongs to her at every state, so far as the portrait gives it: her mother's departure three years earlier, the woman who came to live in the Saitama apartment, the middle school chosen away from her neighborhood, the earlier humiliation and images at school (18.115-146, 18.138-146). Located present states: earlier café visits and the visual-reference scene (10.79, 15.21-110); the train encounter about two weeks before the fifth story, in which she finds the gun (12.289-319, 18.610-664); Introduction 5, the espresso treat and Itō's question (17.36-91); in the fifth story, the threat on the train and the school gate (18.147-223), the tea gathering and payment (18.255-365), the alley and flight from Chisato (18.366-408), Ishihara's assault (18.447-530), the failure to shoot and the attempt on her life (18.550-803), and the café return and 助けて (18.824-875). The split falls at 助けて: before it the conditions below apply; after it only the embrace and her two yeses are observed, and her life after that night is outside the evidence.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The portrait gives a located account: anonymity in Tokyo and recognition at the café (18.34-55, 18.225-252); the café self as real and the school self as the one she feels compelled to play (18.215-223); a treat distinguished from a debt (17.36-72, 18.235-251, 18.824-858); calculation of a tormentor's interests without security (18.147-191); sound distrust that is not foreknowledge (18.255-305); anger with objects and a history (18.99-134). It predicts her mistakes: reading strangers' looks as derision without proof (18.99-112, 18.668-687), reconstructing who has seen which image from fear (18.366-408). Not B: the portrait says the passage cannot settle why she could not shoot the girls or establish a general refusal to do harm (18.695-803); whether her anger or what she sees of the girls decides such a choice is open, which is insufficiency, and her life after the night is withheld. Not D: a dedicated portrait states located conditions for her café conduct, her responses to coercion and her request for help.

Ordered states with triggers: background three years earlier (18.115-146); café visits (10.79, 15.21-110, 17.36-91); the train encounter two weeks before (12.289-319, 18.610-664); the fifth-story day from the train threat to the café return (18.147-875), with the change named by the portrait: the girl who fled Chisato in the alley returns and lets herself be held (18.395-409, 18.839-875). Not B: the endpoint after the night is withheld and the earlier café visits are sparsely placed. Not D: the states and their triggers are located.

The row does not claim speech. The portrait briefly describes register shifts: courteous joking with the adults paying for espresso (17.56-72), faltering when lessons come up (17.56-91), やめて then やめてください when Mizokakushi pretends not to hear (18.163-190), a full indignant sentence that she never ordered the tea (18.329-362), checking anything? and saying 助けて (18.837-875), and inner speech angrier than what she says aloud. Not C: few forms are quoted, the row disclaims speech and the portrait says the printed exchanges give no performed voice. Not E: register shift across conditions is analyzed.

Located habits: saving from the daily allowance, skipping lunches, cheap or given stationery and walking to keep the fare (18.34-55); the espresso treat, disliking bitter tastes and usually avoiding black coffee (17.36-72, 18.824-858); joining a game with Kurumi and posing for Itō's reference scene (15.21-110, 18.228-239); keeping her bag close among people she distrusts (18.255-271). Not B: home and school routines appear only through threat and avoidance. Not D: several distinct habits are located.

The portrait explains how her response changes with whether a relationship imposes scrutiny or debt: Mika as the father she would like, attention without trial; Mizuki's sisterly roughness; Kurumi's games; admiration and a stir at Takina's smile; Chisato as someone she can simply thank, friendship and the wish to be held (18.228-251, 18.395-408, 18.848-875); Itō's innocent question freezing her (17.36-91); Yoneoka answered with a joke (17.56-72); Mizokakushi's 'friend' as power and a nod under threat (18.147-191); Kadowaki met with a precise protest and payment under threat (18.329-362); Ishihara, pleasure at the ride, almost telling him, then resistance (18.447-530); a discriminating account of the woman at home (18.115-137). Not A: café relations are sampled in one or two scenes each, she admits her talk with Chisato contained lies (18.395-408), and her parents' sides are inaccessible. Not C: the differences are located with what produces them.

The fifth story renders her private reasoning: correcting which self is played (18.215-223), fears about her mother (18.115-146), why she vomits and why she cries (18.366-408), her reckoning of anger and her shifting explanations for not shooting (18.99-134, 18.695-803), the smell of coffee before the attempt (18.787-803), and the question anything? (18.837-858). Not A: the narration breaks around the shot, she never hears the adults' account of the protection, and the earlier visits are seen from outside. Not C: her reasoning is located at each turn.

Located: やめて then the added ください and a nod to an invitation she tried to refuse (18.147-191); pretending to drink and keeping her bag close (18.255-305); a precise protest, payment under threat and the question whether Kadowaki will admit the price was a lie (18.329-362); recoiling and escaping at the lift (18.366-408); active physical resistance to Ishihara (18.487-530); not shooting her tormentors (18.695-780). Not B: the conflict with the weapon is the one the portrait leaves unsettled. Not D: many conflicts are located with their conditions.

The row claims ethics. Located weighing: the woman at home may not be a bad person yet Kana hates sharing her home (18.115-137); she treats the gun as a means of regaining power over her future (18.610-664); she calls up hypothetical future victims to justify shooting, fails, and calls herself a coward (18.720-780). Not B: why she could not shoot is unsettled, and whether she would have agreed to the steps taken before her request is unknown (18.850-875). Not D: actual weighing is located.

Located: the invitation to the adults to treat her any time, with theatrical timing (17.36-72); reported participation in café jokes and liking Kurumi's fallibility in games of reading people (18.225-239). Not C: one located joke and reported participation. Not E: the portrait analyzes her timing and wit.

The portrait covers her appearances across Ordinary days with spine-and-paragraph locators and keeps others' accounts attributed: Mizuki's, Mika's and Kurumi's report of the protection, the rumor about Ishihara's earlier school, the fugitive's view on the train, Tokuda's view of the café. Not A: one derived item; speech is not claimed and only briefly described. Not C: her whole appearance is located and attributed.

Located bounds against overreading: her parents' histories are inaccessible and her father's image is the future she expects (18.115-137, 18.770-779); her confusion at Kadowaki's touch is not a wish for his attention (18.309-331); her distrust is vindicated without foreknowledge (18.255-305); the train encounter is not a gift from the café (12.289-319, 18.610-664); Ishihara's earlier conduct is a rumor (18.141-146); not shooting is not a general refusal to do harm, and her survival is not assigned to her actions alone (18.695-803); who attached the voucher and how she survived are not witnessed (18.787-837); image deletion is expected, not verified, no Lycoris job is offered and the last arrival is not her (18.883-910, 19.69-78); attraction to Takina assigns no orientation (18.228-239). Not A: no forecast is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

Intervals are located: three years since her mother left, about two weeks since the train encounter, and the fifth-story day ordered by paragraph into the night. Not B: no calendar dates, and the earlier café visits are not placed exactly. Not D: the order is located.

scenario_readiness.note: The row does not claim speech; the portrait describes her register shifts only briefly, quotes few forms, and says the printed exchanges give no performed voice.

conditions: An invitation at her own pace in established café company, with no unwanted debt: predict curiosity, questions about what she does not know, accepting a treat with thanks and a joke, and a return visit (17.36-72, 18.225-252, 18.824-875).
An innocent question about why she comes to Tokyo or about her lessons: predict that she freezes or falters and deflects (17.36-91).

A demand to pay for what she did not order, or coercion backed by a threat to expose her: predict a precise protest, then compliance under the threat; a nod or silence under threat does not signify willingness (18.147-191, 18.329-362).
Something supplied by people she distrusts: predict that she pretends to consume it and keeps her belongings close (18.255-305).

Include her mistakes: reading strangers' looks as derision without proof (18.99-112, 18.668-687); reconstructing from fear who has seen what (18.366-408); offering café companions a partly invented account of herself (18.395-408).

Exclude any re-staging of the assault, the weapon or self-harm, which are exceptional states and not a transferable policy; whether she would act on her anger; her life after the night at home, at school or with the police; romance; and anything that needs a performed voice.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Ordinary days from the earlier café visits to the fifth-story night, split at 助けて: the conditions draw on states before her request, and after it only the embrace and her two yeses are observed.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Café staff and regulars as established company (Mika, Mizuki, Kurumi, Takina, Chisato, Itō, Yoneoka); Mizokakushi and Kadowaki as coercers. Unknown adults and new peers are not covered; a comparable new café regular is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: Café LycoReco and the trains between Saitama and Tokyo, with the school gate only as a setting of threat.
No television identity, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation from the portrait's closing paragraphs and the located acts they rest on. Her life after the night and the choice the portrait leaves unsettled are excluded.

conditions: Café counter settings with staff and regulars: listening, asking, joining a joke, accepting a treat, frugal travel and food choices (17.36-72, 18.34-55, 18.225-252).
Excluded: home routines, school peers outside the coercion, and any social circle outside the café.
scenario_readiness.note: Her café life is well located; her home and school life appear only through threat and avoidance.
Her central deliberation, whether to shoot, is located but its deciding motive is unsettled by the portrait, which says the passage cannot establish a general refusal to do harm (18.695-803).
She is a middle-school pupil; the portrait differentiates admiration for Takina from affection for Chisato and expressly assigns no orientation or reciprocal feeling (18.228-251).
She has no work; school appears only as a setting of coercion and a teacher's misjudgment (18.199-223).

known_limits.statement: The portrait says the passage cannot establish a general refusal to do harm or settle why she could not shoot the girls; her explanations shift with the danger, the memory and what she sees (18.695-803).
What she finds at home, at school, with the police or on her next trip to Tokyo is unknown, and there is no later scene in which she judges the steps taken for her (18.850-910).
The adults' and Kurumi's account of the surveillance and intervention is not heard by her, and their claims about the deletion and DA operation are not verified (18.567-605, 18.877-905).
She admits her side of the café conversation with Chisato contained quite a few lies, so her café self-reports are not facts about her life (18.395-408).
Her stir at Takina's smile and her affection for Chisato are differentiated feelings; the portrait assigns no orientation and no reciprocal feeling (18.228-251).

The assault, the weapon and the attempt on her life are exceptional states; behavior in them is not generalized into a transferable policy, and her survival is not assigned to her actions alone (18.447-530, 18.787-837).
Speech is not claimed on the row and the portrait gives no performed voice, so no register can be modeled beyond the few located forms.
Untested: a return visit after the night, contact with her family or teachers after the rescue, and new peers.
